description: We are a team of four Informatics students passionate about technology, data science, and solving real-world challenges. Through FireWatch, we aim to transform MODIS and VIIRS satellite observations into meaningful fire intelligence. We are interested in software development, AI, and Earth observation.
summary: Pyroscope is a wildfire-monitoring tool that combines fire detections from two NASA satellite instruments, MODIS and VIIRS, into one consistent picture. The two instruments see the same fires at different resolutions and with different detection rules. That produces overlapping, inconsistent records that are hard to compare across years and countries. Pyroscope merges them into a single harmonized dataset, shows it on an interactive map, and adds a Python forecast model that predicts fire activity country by country instead of as one regional number. It addresses Harmonization of MODIS and VIIRS Hot Spots. It matters because responders, researchers and planners need a trustworthy view of where fire is happening and where it is likely to occur next. Pyroscope uses only open NASA data, so anyone can reproduce it.
details:
What it does. Pyroscope takes NASA FIRMS active-fire detections from MODIS (about 1 km resolution) and VIIRS (375 m) and harmonizes them into one fire record. It displays the result on a web map and forecasts fire activity per country.

How it works.

  1. It ingests FIRMS MODIS and VIIRS detections. Our test dataset covers Egypt, 2015 to 2025.
  2. It aligns the fields of the two sources and merges overlapping detections.
  3. It shows the harmonized data on an interactive map.
  4. A Python model trained on real FIRMS data produces a forecast, displayed as a country-by-country map at the bottom of the page.

Working features and evidence.

  • The harmonization tool exists in two versions: a single-file JavaScript/HTML app and a second version in a project package.
  • Egypt 2015 to 2025 FIRMS data is loaded and harmonized.
